lines.text: Ask your agent for a picture. It writes you a prompt.
Ask it to listen to a recording. It asks you for the transcript.
Ask if its GPU code works. It says it should.
You could give it a GPU yourself.
Open an account. Paste a cloud key into the chat. Install CUDA. Keep an eye on the box.
Then nobody watches it, and the bill keeps running. One developer expected a hundred dollars. The bill was a thousand.
And an agent holding a cloud key with no limits? Someone called that “terrifying.”
GPU for Agents gives it the power, with the controls built in.
Paste one line. The agent rents its own GPU and sets it up in minutes.
Now it makes images and voices.
It transcribes audio on its own GPU, without a third-party API.
It runs open models, under your rules, and tests its own GPU code on real hardware.
Everything sits behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that its tools already call.
You set the budget. The agent sees the price before it rents, and the machine shuts itself down at your cap.
Every step goes into an event log, so you can audit what it did and what it cost.
A watchdog runs inside the machine. When the work stops, the GPU stops.
Even if you closed the chat.
New powers for your agent. And you keep the controls.
